The [official NextItNet implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py) is TensorFlow: its standard residual block applies causal convolution → channel LayerNorm → ReLU twice, with dilations d and 2d, then adds the residual. Each convolution has its own weights and bias; shared-weight branches are a modification. In PyTorch, for B×C×L input and stride 1, use `F.conv1d(F.pad(x, ((k-1)*d, 0)), weight, bias, dilation=d, padding=0)`. Normalize channels independently per timestep using `LayerNorm(C)` on B×L×C; including time in normalization can leak future information. [PyTorch LayerNorm documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.normalization.LayerNorm.html)

Padding recommendation, inferred from these operations: mask embeddings initially and restore zeros at padded positions before every temporal convolution. Biased convolutions and LayerNorm’s learned offset can regenerate nonzero padding, so reapply the mask after each convolution–normalization–activation stage, before the next convolution, and after residual addition/final normalization. For pre-normalization blocks, mask after normalization/activation before convolution. Masking immediately after convolution alone is insufficient if affine normalization follows. Channel-only normalization allows masking after the complete pointwise stage; masking every intermediate operation is unnecessary. This preserves zero-padding semantics; causal convolution alone already prevents future-token access.

Identical dilation implies redundant parallel branches only when inputs, weights, biases, normalization, and stochastic operations also match. Separate dropout calls sample fresh masks—even through the same module—so branches generally differ during training; averaging them changes noise variance and training behavior. Exact collapse requires a shared realized mask or disabled dropout, plus compatible branch aggregation. Equal expected dropout outputs do not establish equivalence through nonlinear downstream layers or losses. [PyTorch Dropout documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Dropout.html)
